name: Tennessee
agency: Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security, Driver Services Division
permitAge: 15 (Level 1 Learner Permit), after written and vision tests (manual p. 14)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified on form SF-1256 signed by a parent, legal guardian or licensed driving instructor (manual p. 14)
teen.nightLimit: Learner permit: no driving 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Intermediate restricted: no driving 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. unless with a parent/guardian or a licensed driver 21+ designated in writing, or for school events, work, or hunting/fishing 4-6 a.m. with written permission/license (manual p. 14, 19)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate restricted: one passenger, unless a passenger is 21+ with a valid license, or siblings going to/from school with a parent letter (manual p. 19)
teen.phone: Learner and intermediate license holders: no cell phone use while driving (manual p. 18). All drivers: hands-free law since 2019, no holding a phone with any part of the body (manual p. 30).

notes: Learner permit holder must have a licensed driver 21+ in the front seat.
Intermediate restricted license at 16 after 180 days on the permit, 50 hours (10 at night) and a road skills test.
Move over (TCA 55-8-132): emergency, tow, highway maintenance, solid waste and utility vehicles; since 2017 any stopped vehicle with flashing lights. Change lanes if safe, otherwise slow down.
School bus on a highway divided by a median or barrier: oncoming traffic need not stop but must go with caution; traffic behind must stop.
Interstate maximum 70 mph reported by secondary sources only; not used in questions.
Intermediate unrestricted license at 17 after holding the restricted license 1 year (90 days more for 6+ points, an at-fault crash or 2 seatbelt violations) (manual p. 14).

Online knowledge test (ages 15-17, proctored by parent/guardian via Proctor ID app): 30 questions, 80% to pass, English and Spanish (tn.gov knowledge-test-online page). The manual does not state the question count or pass mark.
At Driver Service Centers the computerized test is also offered in Spanish, Korean and Japanese; interpreters are not allowed (manual p. 21).
Handbook: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, information current as of July 1, 2022 (PDF last modified 2026-04-23). Printed page = PDF page minus 14. Read 2026-10-09.
Insurance minimum 25/50/25 confirmed on the tn.gov Department of Revenue Financial Responsibility page; not stated in the manual.
